```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(mysteryroster)
```

A registry-validity study asks one question of each physician-location
listing: is the named physician still practising the indexed specialty at the
listed address? This vignette walks the protocol in order with synthetic data.
Section numbers refer to the OB/GYN subspecialty registry-validity protocol
(COMIRB draft, October 2026); the same steps reproduce the ENT study.

## Section 4 and 5: registries, overlap zones, strata

Each registry is a vector or data frame of identifiers. The first registry is
the sampling frame (NPPES in both studies).

```{r overlap}
set.seed(2026)
nppes   <- sprintf("%010d", 1:1200)
board   <- sample(nppes, 700)                       # certified subset
society <- c(sample(board, 300), sample(setdiff(nppes, board), 60))
ov <- registry_overlap(list(nppes = nppes, board = board, society = society))
overlap_zone_counts(ov)
```

Protocol strata A, B, C and D are the frame registry's overlap zones:

```{r strata}
frame <- frame_strata(ov, frame = "nppes")
table(frame$stratum)
```

## Section 5: a stratified sample that keeps its sampling probabilities

Rare zones are oversampled on purpose; the weights make the estimates
representative again.

```{r sample}
listings <- stratified_listing_sample(
  frame,
  allocation = c("nppes" = 60, "nppes+society" = 40, "nppes+board" = 60, "nppes+board+society" = 60),
  seed = 20261009)
attr(listings, "allocation")
```

## Section 7: dispositions become four exhaustive statuses

The disposition map is the study codebook. `ent_disposition_map()` is the ENT
study's REDCap vocabulary; an OB/GYN study passes its own strings in the same
four categories. An unmapped disposition stops the call, so codebook drift
cannot silently become "unresolved".

```{r status}
calls <- listings
calls$reached <- sample(c(TRUE, FALSE, NA), nrow(calls), TRUE, prob = c(0.7, 0.2, 0.1))
calls$disposition <- ifelse(calls$reached %in% TRUE,
  sample(unlist(ent_disposition_map()), nrow(calls), TRUE, prob = c(0.6, 0.1, 0.05, 0.1, 0.1, 0.05)),
  NA)
calls <- classify_listing_status(calls, phone_valid = NULL)
table(calls$listing_status)
```

## Section 9: design-weighted estimates, bounds, model, flow

```{r analysis}
design <- listing_validity_design(calls)
validity_estimates(design)
validity_estimates(design, by = "stratum")
validity_sensitivity_bounds(calls)
validity_model(design, ~ stratum)
listing_flow_counts(calls, by = "stratum")
```

The weighted estimate is the primary estimand (all sampled listings in the
denominator, unresolved reported explicitly). `definitive_only = TRUE` gives
the complete-case estimate, and the bounds table gives the two extreme-case
scenarios the protocol requires alongside it.
